# This file is for running some exloratory analysis code

04/14: Illustrate how Copula works

```{r}
# 1. SETUP AND DATA GENERATION ------------------------------------------------
# Load required libraries
library(MASS)
library(spaMM)   # For the Generalized Linear Geostatistical Model (GLGM)
library(gcKrig)  # For the Gaussian Copula Model
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Generate the 10x10 Forest Grid
set.seed(123)
n_side <- 10
x <- rep(1:n_side, times = n_side)
y <- rep(1:n_side, each = n_side)
coords <- cbind(x, y)

# Create the hidden continuous spatial layer (Exponential correlation)
distance_matrix <- as.matrix(dist(coords))
phi <- 3 
spatial_cov <- exp(-distance_matrix / phi)
hidden_layer <- mvrnorm(n = 1, mu = rep(0, 100), Sigma = spatial_cov)

# Convert to discrete Poisson counts
base_rate <- 2 
lambda <- exp(log(base_rate) + hidden_layer) 
tree_counts <- rpois(n = 100, lambda = lambda)

forest_data <- data.frame(x = x, y = y, trees = tree_counts)

# 2. TRAIN / TEST SPLIT -------------------------------------------------------
# Randomly select 20 locations to "hide" and use for testing
set.seed(42)
test_indices <- sample(1:100, 20)

train_data <- forest_data[-test_indices, ]
test_data  <- forest_data[test_indices, ]

train_coords <- cbind(train_data$x, train_data$y)
test_coords  <- cbind(test_data$x, test_data$y)

# 3. TRAIN MODELS AND PREDICT -------------------------------------------------

# --- Model A: GLGM (The "Hidden Layer" Model) ---
cat("Fitting GLGM...\n")
glgm_model <- fitme(
  trees ~ 1 + Matern(1 | x + y), 
  data = train_data, 
  family = poisson()
)

# Predict GLGM expected counts
# type = "response" ensures the predictions are brought back to the count scale
glgm_preds <- predict(glgm_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")

# --- Model B: Gaussian Copula (gcKrig) ---
cat("Fitting Copula Model...\n")
# Note: For toy speed, we lower the GHK simulation reps. 
# In a real study, increase nrep to c(100, 1000) for higher accuracy.
copula_model <- mlegc(
  y = train_data$trees, 
  locs = train_coords, 
  marginal = poisson.gc(link = "log"), 
  corr = matern.gc(kappa = 0.5, nugget = FALSE), 
  method = "GHK",
  ghkoptions = list(nrep = c(50, 100), reorder = FALSE, seed = 123)
)

cat("Predicting with Copula Model...\n")
copula_preds_obj <- predgc(
  obs.y = train_data$trees,
  obs.locs = train_coords,
  pred.locs = test_coords,
  marginal = poisson.gc(link = "log"),
  corr = matern.gc(kappa = 0.5, nugget = FALSE),
  # Remove the 'estpar' line entirely
  method = "GHK",
  ghkoptions = list(nrep = c(50, 100), reorder = FALSE, seed = 123)
)

# Extract the predicted mean counts
copula_preds <- summary(copula_preds_obj)$predMean


# 4. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION ---------------------------------------------------
# Create a dataframe to compare predictions with the truth
results <- data.frame(
  Location = 1:20,
  True_Count = test_data$trees,
  GLGM_Pred = as.numeric(glgm_preds),
  Copula_Pred = as.numeric(copula_preds)
)

# Calculate Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
glgm_mae <- mean(abs(results$True_Count - results$GLGM_Pred))
copula_mae <- mean(abs(results$True_Count - results$Copula_Pred))

glgm_rmse <- sqrt(mean((results$True_Count - results$GLGM_Pred)^2))
copula_rmse <- sqrt(mean((results$True_Count - results$Copula_Pred)^2))

cat("\n--- PERFORMANCE EVALUATION ---\n")
cat(sprintf("GLGM   - MAE: %.3f | RMSE: %.3f\n", glgm_mae, glgm_rmse))
cat(sprintf("Copula - MAE: %.3f | RMSE: %.3f\n", copula_mae, copula_rmse))


# 5. VISUAL ILLUSTRATION ------------------------------------------------------
# Let's visualize the True vs Predicted values side-by-side using a scatter plot
plot_data <- results %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("GLGM_Pred", "Copula_Pred"), 
               names_to = "Model", 
               values_to = "Prediction")

# Clean up model names for the plot
plot_data$Model <- ifelse(plot_data$Model == "GLGM_Pred", "GLGM", "Copula (gcKrig)")

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = True_Count, y = Prediction, color = Model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") + # The "Perfect Prediction" line
  scale_color_manual(values = c("GLGM" = "#E69F00", "Copula (gcKrig)" = "#56B4E9")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Prediction Accuracy: True vs. Predicted Tree Counts",
    subtitle = "Points closer to the dashed line indicate better predictions",
    x = "True Observed Count (Hold-out Test Set)",
    y = "Predicted Count"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
```

```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ZERO-COMPUTATION HEATMAPS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(ggplot2)

# 1. STITCH PREDICTIONS BACK INTO THE GRID
# Create copies of the original forest_data
grid_glgm <- forest_data
grid_copula <- forest_data

# Overwrite ONLY the 20 hidden "test" locations with the models' predictions
grid_glgm$trees[test_indices] <- as.numeric(glgm_preds)
grid_copula$trees[test_indices] <- as.numeric(copula_preds)


# 2. CREATE A SIMPLE PLOTTING FUNCTION
# This keeps the code short and clean
plot_simple_heatmap <- function(data_to_plot, title_text) {
  ggplot(data_to_plot, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = trees)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    
    # Add the numbers on top (rounded to 1 decimal for predictions)
    geom_text(aes(label = round(trees, 1)), size = 3.5,
              color = ifelse(data_to_plot$trees > mean(data_to_plot$trees), "white", "black")) +
    
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", name = "Tree Count") +
    coord_fixed() + 
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = title_text, x = "X", y = "Y") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
          panel.grid = element_blank())
}


# 3. PRINT THE THREE PLOTS (Safely!)
# Run these one by one in your console

# Plot 1: The absolute truth (all 100 points)
plot_1 <- plot_simple_heatmap(forest_data, "1. True Data")
print(plot_1)

# Plot 2: GLGM (80 True + 20 Predicted)
plot_2 <- plot_simple_heatmap(grid_glgm, "2. GLGM (80 True + 20 Predicted)")
print(plot_2)

# Plot 3: gcKrig (80 True + 20 Predicted)
plot_3 <- plot_simple_heatmap(grid_copula, "3. gcKrig (80 True + 20 Predicted)")
print(plot_3)
```

Another simple example of spatial count data and using gcKrig

```{r}
# install.packages(c("gcKrig", "ggplot2", "patchwork"))

library(gcKrig)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

set.seed(1234)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. create a simple spatial grid
# ------------------------------------------------------------

grid <- seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.1)
locs <- expand.grid(x = grid, y = grid)

n_all <- nrow(locs)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. generate one simple spatial count dataset
#    true model:
#    - negative binomial marginal
#    - mean depends on x and y
#    - matern spatial correlation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

mu_true <- exp(1 + 0.8 * locs$x - 0.8 * locs$y)

sim_obj <- simgc(
  locs = as.matrix(locs),
  sim.n = 1,
  marginal = negbin.gc(mu = mu_true, od = 0.6),
  corr = matern.gc(range = 0.25, kappa = 0.5, nugget = 0.05)
)

y_all <- sim_obj$data
if (is.matrix(y_all)) {
  y_all <- y_all[, 1]
}

full_df <- data.frame(
  x = locs$x,
  y = locs$y,
  true_count = y_all
)

# extract simulated counts robustly
if (is.matrix(sim_obj$data) || is.data.frame(sim_obj$data)) {
  y_all <- as.numeric(sim_obj$data[, 1])
} else {
  y_all <- as.numeric(sim_obj$data)
}

length(y_all)
nrow(locs)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. split into observed and hidden locations
# ------------------------------------------------------------

obs_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_all), size = 70, replace = FALSE)
pred_idx <- setdiff(seq_len(n_all), obs_idx)

obs_locs <- as.matrix(locs[obs_idx, c("x", "y")])
pred_locs <- as.matrix(locs[pred_idx, c("x", "y")])

obs_x <- as.matrix(locs[obs_idx, c("x", "y")])
pred_x <- as.matrix(locs[pred_idx, c("x", "y")])

obs_y <- y_all[obs_idx]
true_hidden <- y_all[pred_idx]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. fit gcKrig on observed data and predict hidden locations
#    we use the correct marginal family here on purpose
#    to test the basic workflow first
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pred_fit <- predgc(
  obs.y = obs_y,
  obs.x = obs_x,
  obs.locs = obs_locs,
  pred.x = pred_x,
  pred.locs = pred_locs,
  marginal = negbin.gc(link = "log"),
  corr = matern.gc(kappa = 0.5, nugget = TRUE),
  method = "GHK",
  parallel = FALSE,
  ghkoptions = list(nrep = c(100, 300), reorder = FALSE, seed = 1234)
)

pred_sum <- summary(pred_fit)

pred_df <- data.frame(
  x = pred_locs[, 1],
  y = pred_locs[, 2],
  true_count = true_hidden,
  pred_mean = pred_sum$predMean,
  pred_count = pred_sum$predCount,
  pred_var = pred_sum$predVar
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. simple numerical performance summaries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

rmse_mean <- sqrt(mean((pred_df$pred_mean - pred_df$true_count)^2))
mae_mean <- mean(abs(pred_df$pred_mean - pred_df$true_count))

rmse_discrete <- sqrt(mean((pred_df$pred_count - pred_df$true_count)^2))
mae_discrete <- mean(abs(pred_df$pred_count - pred_df$true_count))

cat("RMSE using predictive mean:", round(rmse_mean, 3), "\n")
cat("MAE using predictive mean :", round(mae_mean, 3), "\n")
cat("RMSE using discrete predictor:", round(rmse_discrete, 3), "\n")
cat("MAE using discrete predictor :", round(mae_discrete, 3), "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. create fields for plotting
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_df <- full_df
plot_df$observed <- FALSE
plot_df$observed[obs_idx] <- TRUE

# predicted field:
# - keep observed sites at their true counts
# - fill hidden sites with predicted discrete responses
plot_df$predicted_field <- plot_df$true_count
plot_df$predicted_field[pred_idx] <- pred_df$pred_count

# absolute error only on hidden sites
plot_df$abs_error_hidden <- NA_real_
plot_df$abs_error_hidden[pred_idx] <- abs(pred_df$pred_count - pred_df$true_count)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. plots
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p1 <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x, y, fill = true_count)) +
  geom_tile() +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "True simulated count field",
    fill = "count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x, y, fill = predicted_field)) +
  geom_tile() +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "Observed + gcKrig predicted field",
    fill = "count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p3 <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x, y, fill = abs_error_hidden)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey85") +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Absolute error on hidden locations",
    fill = "|error|"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p4 <- ggplot(pred_df, aes(true_count, pred_count)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 2, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Hidden locations: true vs predicted",
    x = "true hidden count",
    y = "predicted hidden count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

(p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4)
```

### Example of how Copula method works (not gcKrig)

```{r}
# =========================================================
# example: how a copula reconstructs a bivariate distribution
# =========================================================

# packages
library(copula)
library(MASS)

set.seed(123)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. define the true joint distribution
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# true dependence: Gaussian copula with rho = 0.7
true_rho <- 0.7
true_cop <- normalCopula(param = true_rho, dim = 2)

# true marginals:
# x1 ~ Gamma(shape = 2, rate = 1)
# x2 ~ Lognormal(meanlog = 0.5, sdlog = 0.6)
true_mvdc <- mvdc(
  copula = true_cop,
  margins = c("gamma", "lnorm"),
  paramMargins = list(
    list(shape = 2, rate = 1),
    list(meanlog = 0.5, sdlog = 0.6)
  )
)

# simulate "observed" data from the true model
n <- 1000
x <- rMvdc(n, true_mvdc)
colnames(x) <- c("x1", "x2")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. visualize the true simulated data
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# helper function: draw 2d kernel density contour
plot_density_contour <- function(data, main_title) {
  kd <- kde2d(data[, 1], data[, 2], n = 100)
  contour(kd,
          main = main_title,
          xlab = "x1",
          ylab = "x2",
          drawlabels = FALSE)
}

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

plot(x[, 1], x[, 2],
     pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
     xlab = "x1", ylab = "x2",
     main = "true simulated data")

hist(x[, 1], breaks = 30, main = "true x1 marginal", xlab = "x1")
hist(x[, 2], breaks = 30, main = "true x2 marginal", xlab = "x2")

plot_density_contour(x, "true joint density contour")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. fit marginal distributions separately
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# fit x1 with Gamma by MLE
fit_x1 <- fitdistr(x[, 1], densfun = "gamma")
shape_hat <- fit_x1$estimate["shape"]
rate_hat  <- fit_x1$estimate["rate"]

# fit x2 with Lognormal by MLE
fit_x2 <- fitdistr(x[, 2], densfun = "lognormal")
meanlog_hat <- fit_x2$estimate["meanlog"]
sdlog_hat   <- fit_x2$estimate["sdlog"]

cat("estimated marginal parameters:\n")
cat("x1 gamma shape =", shape_hat, ", rate =", rate_hat, "\n")
cat("x2 lognormal meanlog =", meanlog_hat, ", sdlog =", sdlog_hat, "\n\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. transform data to pseudo-uniforms using fitted marginals
# ---------------------------------------------------------

u1_hat <- pgamma(x[, 1], shape = shape_hat, rate = rate_hat)
u2_hat <- plnorm(x[, 2], meanlog = meanlog_hat, sdlog = sdlog_hat)

u_hat <- cbind(u1_hat, u2_hat)

# avoid exact 0 or 1 for numerical stability
eps <- 1e-6
u_hat[u_hat < eps] <- eps
u_hat[u_hat > 1 - eps] <- 1 - eps

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. fit Gaussian copula to the transformed uniforms
# ---------------------------------------------------------

fit_cop <- fitCopula(
  normalCopula(param = 0.3, dim = 2),
  data = u_hat,
  method = "ml"
)

rho_hat <- coef(fit_cop)[1]

cat("true copula rho =", true_rho, "\n")
cat("estimated copula rho =", rho_hat, "\n\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 6. construct the fitted joint model
# ---------------------------------------------------------

fitted_cop <- normalCopula(param = rho_hat, dim = 2)

fitted_mvdc <- mvdc(
  copula = fitted_cop,
  margins = c("gamma", "lnorm"),
  paramMargins = list(
    list(shape = shape_hat, rate = rate_hat),
    list(meanlog = meanlog_hat, sdlog = sdlog_hat)
  )
)

# simulate from the fitted copula model
x_hat <- rMvdc(n, fitted_mvdc)
colnames(x_hat) <- c("x1", "x2")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 7. compare true data and fitted-copula-generated data
# ---------------------------------------------------------

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

plot(x[, 1], x[, 2],
     pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
     xlab = "x1", ylab = "x2",
     main = "true simulated data")

plot(x_hat[, 1], x_hat[, 2],
     pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
     xlab = "x1", ylab = "x2",
     main = "data from fitted copula model")

plot_density_contour(x, "true joint density contour")
plot_density_contour(x_hat, "fitted joint density contour")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 8. optional: compare the copula layer directly
# ---------------------------------------------------------

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(u_hat[, 1], u_hat[, 2],
     pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
     xlab = "u1_hat", ylab = "u2_hat",
     main = "estimated uniforms from data")

u_sim <- rCopula(n, fitted_cop)
plot(u_sim[, 1], u_sim[, 2],
     pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
     xlab = "u1", ylab = "u2",
     main = "simulated uniforms from fitted copula")
```

04/14: Replicate Paper's figure 1

```{r}
install.packages("gcKrig")
library(gcKrig)

# Simulate a spatial count dataset (from the paper's Figure 1)
xloc <- seq(0, 1, length = 10)
yloc <- seq(0, 1, length = 10)
locs <- expand.grid(xloc, yloc)

sim1 <- simgc(locs = cbind(locs[,1], locs[,2]), sim.n = 1,
              marginal = negbin.gc(mu = 5, od = 1),
              corr = matern.gc(range = 0.3, kappa = 0.5, nugget = 0.1))
```



```{r}
###############################################################################
# Replication of Han & De Oliveira (2018), Section 5 / Table 3
# 
# This script reproduces the package comparison simulation from the gcKrig
# paper. It simulates a spatial count dataset on an 11x11 grid from a 
# Gaussian copula model with:
#   - Negative binomial marginals (with covariates)
#   - Exponential correlation function (Matern with kappa = 0.5, no nugget)
#
# True parameters:
#   beta0 = 1 (intercept), beta1 = 0.5 (covariate xloc), beta2 = 1 (covariate yloc)
#   sigma^2 = 1 (overdispersion), range = 0.3
#
# The model is fit using gcKrig with both GHK and GQT methods, and we compare
# parameter estimates, standard errors, log-likelihoods, and computation times.
###############################################################################

# ---- Load package ----
library(gcKrig)

# ---- Step 1: Set up the spatial grid ----
# 11 x 11 regular grid on [0,1]^2 => 121 locations
xloc <- rep(seq(0, 1, by = 0.1), 11)
yloc <- rep(seq(0, 1, by = 0.1), each = 11)

# Distance matrix (used later for mvtnorm comparison)
simD <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(xloc, yloc)))

# ---- Step 2: Simulate data ----
# True parameters:
#   log(mu(s)) = beta0 + beta1 * xloc + beta2 * yloc
#   beta0 = 1, beta1 = 0.5, beta2 = 1
#   overdispersion (od) = 1
#   Matern correlation with range = 0.3, kappa = 0.5 (exponential), no nugget
set.seed(321)
simData1 <- simgc(
  locs = cbind(xloc, yloc), 
  sim.n = 1,
  marginal = negbin.gc(mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * xloc + yloc), od = 1),
  corr = matern.gc(range = 0.3, nugget = 0)
)

# Create data frame for model fitting
simDf1 <- data.frame(xloc = xloc, yloc = yloc, data = simData1$data)

cat("=== Simulated Data Summary ===\n")
cat("Number of locations:", nrow(simDf1), "\n")
cat("Count range:", range(simDf1$data), "\n")
cat("Count mean:", round(mean(simDf1$data), 2), "\n\n")

# ---- Step 3: Fit using gcKrig - GHK method ----
cat("Fitting gcKrig with GHK method...\n")
t0 <- proc.time()
gcKrigGHK <- mlegc(
  y = simDf1[, 3], 
  x = simDf1[, 1:2],
  locs = cbind(xloc, yloc), 
  method = "GHK",
  marginal = negbin.gc(link = "log"),
  corr = matern.gc(nugget = FALSE),
  ghkoptions = list(nrep = c(100, 1000), seed = 123)
)
tgcKrigGHK <- proc.time() - t0
cat("  Done in", round(tgcKrigGHK["elapsed"], 1), "seconds\n\n")

# ---- Step 4: Fit using gcKrig - GQT method ----
cat("Fitting gcKrig with GQT method...\n")
t0 <- proc.time()
gcKrigGQT <- mlegc(
  y = simDf1[, 3], 
  x = simDf1[, 1:2],
  locs = cbind(xloc, yloc), 
  method = "GQT",
  marginal = negbin.gc(link = "log"),
  corr = matern.gc(nugget = FALSE)
)
tgcKrigGQT <- proc.time() - t0
cat("  Done in", round(tgcKrigGQT["elapsed"], 1), "seconds\n\n")

# ---- Step 5: Extract and compare results ----
cat("=============================================\n")
cat("  Replication of Han (2018) Table 3\n")
cat("=============================================\n\n")

# Extract estimates and standard errors
ghk_est <- summary(gcKrigGHK)
gqt_est <- summary(gcKrigGQT)

# The summary object structure may vary; print the full summaries
cat("--- gcKrig GHK Summary ---\n")
print(summary(gcKrigGHK))
cat("\n--- gcKrig GQT Summary ---\n")
print(summary(gcKrigGQT))

cat("\n=============================================\n")
cat("  Comparison Table\n")
cat("=============================================\n\n")

# True parameter values for reference
true_params <- c(beta0 = 1.0, beta1 = 0.5, beta2 = 1.0, sigma2 = 1.0, range = 0.3)
cat("True parameters:\n")
print(true_params)

cat("\nTiming comparison:\n")
cat("  GHK:", round(tgcKrigGHK["elapsed"], 1), "seconds\n")
cat("  GQT:", round(tgcKrigGQT["elapsed"], 1), "seconds\n")

# ---- Step 6: Visualize the simulated data ----
cat("\n\nGenerating visualization of simulated data...\n")
pdf("simulated_data_plot.pdf", width = 10, height = 4)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))

# Plot 1: Counts at locations
plot(xloc, yloc, cex = 0.5 + simDf1$data / max(simDf1$data) * 2,
     pch = 19, col = "steelblue",
     main = "Simulated Counts (size ~ count)",
     xlab = "xloc", ylab = "yloc")

# Plot 2: Histogram of counts
hist(simDf1$data, breaks = 20, col = "lightblue", border = "white",
     main = "Distribution of Counts", xlab = "Count", ylab = "Frequency")
abline(v = mean(simDf1$data), col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

# Plot 3: True mean surface
mu_true <- exp(1 + 0.5 * xloc + yloc)
plot(xloc, yloc, cex = 0.5 + mu_true / max(mu_true) * 2,
     pch = 19, col = "darkorange",
     main = "True Mean Surface (size ~ mu)",
     xlab = "xloc", ylab = "yloc")

dev.off()
cat("Plot saved to simulated_data_plot.pdf\n")

cat("\n=== Script complete ===\n")
cat("This replicates the core workflow of Han (2018) Section 5.\n")
cat("The exact numbers will differ slightly from the paper due to\n")
cat("platform-specific RNG behavior, but the overall pattern should match.\n")
```

### 3.1 Simulate data using gcKrig

```{r}
# Load the package
library(gcKrig)

# 1. Create a 10x10 spatial grid of locations
grid <- seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.1)
xloc <- expand.grid(x = grid, y = grid)[, 1]
yloc <- expand.grid(x = grid, y = grid)[, 2]

# 2. Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(12345)

# 3. Simulate the spatial count data
# We specify a Negative Binomial marginal (mean = 5, overdispersion = 1)
# We specify a Matern correlation (range = 0.3, kappa = 0.5, nugget = 0.1)
sim1 <- simgc(locs = cbind(xloc, yloc), sim.n = 1,
              marginal = negbin.gc(mu = 5, od = 1),
              corr = matern.gc(range = 0.3, kappa = 0.5, nugget = 0.1))

# 4. Visualize the data (will output a grid with exact text counts)
plot(sim1, index = 1, plottype = "Text", col = 2)

# You can also view it as a 3D scatter plot
plot(sim1, index = 1, plottype = "3D", col = 2)
```

### Atlantic Fish

```{r}
# Load the built-in dataset
data("AtlanticFish", package = "gcKrig")

# Fit the Gaussian Copula Model using the GHK simulator
Fitfish <- mlegc(y = AtlanticFish[, 3], 
                 x = AtlanticFish[, 4:7],
                 locs = AtlanticFish[, 1:2], 
                 longlat = TRUE,
                 marginal = negbin.gc(link = "log"),
                 corr = matern.gc(kappa = 0.5, nugget = TRUE), 
                 method = "GHK")

# Review the parameter estimates and standard errors
summary(Fitfish)
```
